notes: Adds a fairly elaborate collector and exports a configs helper, yet any parent claim still drops every child block for the same ConfigResource, so partial overrides are lost; it also edits CHANGELOG.md.

Fixes the reported root-module case, but it still dedups at config time. A parent block silently drops every child-module block for that resource, and a static block plus a for_each block on the same resource in one module now drops one of them, the same class of silent loss as the bug; it also exports a configs function and edits CHANGELOG.

Fixes the root-level bug and handles static per-instance parent/child overrides, but deduplicating before expansion is complex and fragile: an unkeyed module shim or a dynamic for_each block in the parent still silently drops child blocks for other instances, and it edits CHANGELOG.md directly.

Keeps all same-module blocks and does per-instance parent override when both addresses are statically parseable. It still resolves overrides at config time, so for_each import blocks across modules are dropped wholesale (likely the failing hidden test); tests are thorough, including a unit fixture, count, and apply.

A simple, minimal fix for the reported same-module case, but cross-module override stays at ConfigResource granularity, so a parent block targeting one instance silently discards all of the child's blocks for that resource (the same class of bug).

A simple fix that keeps all blocks from the same module, which resolves the reported issue. A parent-module block still discards all child-module blocks for that resource rather than only the overlapping instance, which is why it fails the hidden module-override tests.

Matches the reference approach (returns all statements, dedups per expanded instance with parent-first precedence), plus defensible but unrequested ctx-shadowing and slice-aliasing cleanups; it has only one regression test and no module-override test.

Matches the reference design: FindImportStatements returns all statements and dedup happens per resolved instance at expansion time (first wins, parent first). The ctx-shadowing refactor and the cfg.Path aliasing guard are reasonable but unrelated, and the single test covers only the root-module for_each case.
